title: 17 fishermen held inside Tubbataha protected reef
summary: Seventeen fishermen aboard the fishing boat Bea Vin 1 were apprehended for unauthorized entry into Jessie Beazley Reef, a protected coral cay of the Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea. Liveaboard dive vessels RV Philippine Siren 2 and MY Resolute alerted authorities to the boat's presence. Tubbataha Management Office rangers, the Philippine Coast Guard, the Philippine Navy and the Cagayancillo local government carried out the apprehension, and the PCG transported the fishermen to Puerto Princesa City for investigation.

timeline.actor: Tubbataha Management Office, PCG, Philippine Navy, LGU Cagayancillo
timeline.note: Seventeen fishermen on board Bea Vin 1 were apprehended at Jessie Beazley Reef after liveaboard vessels alerted authorities.
The PCG transported the fishermen to Puerto Princesa City, where an investigation was conducted.

title: Pregnant dugong washes up dead in Sarangani Bay
summary: A dugong weighing an estimated 400 to 500 kilograms washed ashore dead in General Santos City on 7 February 2026, within the Sarangani Bay Protected Seascape. A necropsy found the internal organs normal, no foreign objects and no ingested material that could explain the death, but confirmed the animal was carrying a calf and may have been near delivery. The cause of death was left undetermined; the protected area office notes fewer than 200 dugongs are estimated to remain in Philippine waters.
referredTo: Sarangani Bay Protected Seascape Protected Area Management Office (DENR)

timeline.note: A 400 to 500 kilogram dugong was found lifeless on the General Santos City shoreline of Sarangani Bay.

timeline.actor: PAMO-SBPS and Marine Wildlife Rescue Center
timeline.note: A necropsy found no direct cause of death but confirmed the dugong was pregnant.

title: Adult dugong found dead in Sebaste a day after Caluya rescue
summary: An adult dugong was found dead along the shoreline of Barangay Aras-Asan, Sebaste, Antique on the morning of 7 September 2026, and authorities examined the carcass and arranged its handling. A fisheries technologist said the cause of death cannot be established without a necropsy, which could show fishing-related injury, vessel strike, debris or disease. The day before, residents on Liwagao Island in Barangay Sibolo, Caluya, returned a stranded juvenile dugong to the sea at low tide; authorities said there was no indication the two incidents were related.

timeline.note: A juvenile dugong stranded at low tide on Liwagao Island was helped back into the sea.
An adult dugong was found dead on the Aras-Asan shoreline and authorities examined the carcass to determine cause of death.

title: 16 boxes of blast-caught fish seized at Cebu City port
summary: A joint operation at a Cebu City port on 11 August 2026 intercepted 16 boxes of assorted fish believed to have been caught with explosives; the shipment came from Isabela, Basilan. Samples showed positive signs of blast fishing. The Cebu City Bantay Dagat Commission worked with BFAR, the city Department of Veterinary Medicine and Fisheries, the Philippine Coast Guard and PNP Maritime Police, and the fish were turned over to the Maritime Police for documentation and case build-up under fisheries laws.
referredTo: PNP Maritime Police, with BFAR Region VII

timeline.actor: Cebu City Bantay Dagat Commission, BFAR, DVMF, PCG, PNP Maritime
timeline.note: Sixteen boxes of fish showing signs of dynamite fishing were seized at a Cebu City port.
The seized fish were turned over to the Maritime Police for evidence processing and investigation under fisheries laws.

title: Stranded Risso's dolphin dies after rescue in Paoay
summary: A sub-adult Risso's dolphin (Grampus griseus) was rescued off Barangay Masintoc, Paoay on 6 March 2026 after observers noted unstable buoyancy and difficulty breathing. Local authorities and volunteers cared for it, but the dolphin died on 7 March and the carcass was sent to the Mariano Marcos State University laboratory for necropsy. It was the third marine mammal stranding in Region I in 2026, after a dolphin died on 7 January in Alaminos City and another was found dead on 27 February in Santiago, Ilocos Sur; the Philippine Marine Mammal Stranding Network has linked hearing loss in stranded mammals to blast fishing along the Ilocos coast.

timeline.actor: Volunteers, BFAR, PCG and Barangay Masintoc responders
timeline.note: The dolphin was rescued in shallow water off Masintoc and placed under supportive care.
The dolphin died despite four days of rehabilitation efforts.
The carcass was taken to the MMSU laboratory for a necropsy to determine the cause of death.

sources.title: Stranded Risso's dolphin in Ilocos Norte dies despite rehab efforts

title: Whale shark freed from fishing net off Gonzaga
summary: A whale shark (butanding) was accidentally caught in a fishing net in Barangay Caroan, Gonzaga, Cagayan on 14 May 2026. Fishermen worked together to free it and led it back to deeper water with a motorboat; it appeared unharmed. It was the second whale shark rescue in Gonzaga in under a month, after residents returned a stranded whale shark to the sea at Batangan on 22 April.

timeline.note: A whale shark stranded along the Batangan shoreline was returned to the sea using a motorboat.
A whale shark caught in a fishing net was freed and guided back into deeper waters.

title: 50 smuggled endangered tortoises seized at NAIA
summary: On 12 June 2026, Bureau of Customs officers at Ninoy Aquino International Airport found 50 live Radiated and Indian Star tortoises, both CITES-listed species, concealed in the luggage of a Malaysian passenger arriving from Bangkok after x-ray screening flagged the bag. The tortoises were documented, inventoried and turned over to the DENR for custody. The passenger was held for inquest under Republic Act 9147 (Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act) and the Customs Modernization and Tariff Act.
referredTo: DENR (custody of wildlife); Bureau of Customs NAIA (inquest)

timeline.note: Fifty live tortoises were discovered in an arriving passenger's luggage during physical examination.

timeline.actor: BOC with DENR and Bureau of Animal Industry
timeline.note: The tortoises were turned over to DENR and the passenger was subjected to inquest for violating RA 9147 and the CMTA.

title: 140 hawksbill hatchlings released on Pandilusan Island
summary: DENR Region 9, through CENRO Imelda, released 140 critically endangered hawksbill sea turtle hatchlings (Eretmochelys imbricata) on Pandilusan Island, Payao, Zamboanga Sibugay on 19 July 2026. The clutch had been laid on the island's beach and was translocated to a safer spot after high tide threatened the original nest. The municipal government of Payao, the island caretaker, the 106th Infantry Battalion and the Coast Guard Sub-Station in Payao took part in the release.

timeline.actor: DENR-9 CENRO Imelda with LGU Payao, 106th Infantry Battalion and CGSS Payao
timeline.note: One hundred forty hawksbill hatchlings from a translocated nest were released into the sea at Pandilusan Island.

title: 16-foot whale shark found dead with head wound in Kinoguitan
summary: A whale shark (Rhincodon typus) about 16 feet long was found dead and stranded in the shallows at Purok 1, Barangay Bolisong, Kinoguitan, Misamis Oriental on a Saturday, after residents alerted authorities. DENR Region X through CENRO Gingoog City, the Philippine Coast Guard, BFAR and the Kinoguitan LGU inspected the carcass and noted a wound roughly seven inches deep near the head; the cause of death was not determined. BFAR advised immediate burial to prevent sanitation problems from decomposition on the beach.
referredTo: DENR Region X (CENRO Gingoog City) and BFAR

timeline.note: Concerned citizens reported a dead whale shark stranded in the shallow part of the beach.

timeline.actor: DENR X, CENRO Gingoog City, PCG, BFAR and LGU Kinoguitan
timeline.note: Inspection found a roughly seven-inch-deep wound near the head; cause of death was undetermined.

title: Philippine pangolin found in Mendez home bound for Palawan
summary: A resident of Barangay Galicia 3, Mendez, Cavite found a Philippine pangolin roaming inside his house on Wednesday, 2 September 2026, and reported it to the municipal environment office. The animal was turned over to the DENR Biodiversity Management Bureau's Wildlife Resources Conservation Division, which found it had not been kept in captivity and requires a diet of termites and ants. The pangolin, listed as endangered under DENR Administrative Order 2019-09, is being transported to Palawan for rehabilitation before release to its natural habitat; the species is found only in Palawan.

timeline.actor: Resident of Barangay Galicia 3 and Mendez municipal environment office
timeline.note: A pangolin was found inside a house in Galicia 3 and reported to the municipal environment office.
The pangolin was turned over to the BMB for assessment and proper disposition.
DENR arranged transport of the pangolin to Palawan for care and rehabilitation before release.
